items.readable_text:
Content:
The expected value (also known as the expectation or mean) of a discrete random variable is the average value we'd expect to get if we observed the random variable many times.

Content:
For a discrete random variable [MATH: X] with probability mass function [MATH: f(x)] defined over a set [MATH: S,] we can calculate the expected value using the following formula:

Content:
[MATH: \textrm E[X] = \sum\limits_{x \in S} x \cdot f(x)]

Content:
In other words, the expected value is the sum of products of each value of [MATH: X] and its associated probability, taken over all possible values of [MATH: X.]

sections.normalized_html: What is the expected value of one roll of a tetrahedral die?
sections.readable_text: What is the expected value of one roll of a tetrahedral die?

sections.normalized_html:
The expected value of a discrete random variable [MATH: X] with probability mass function [MATH: f(x)] defined over a set [MATH: S] is given by

[MATH: \textrm E[X] = \sum\limits_{x \in S} x \cdot f(x).]

A tetrahedral die has four sides. Let [MATH: X] be the score attained on a random roll of the die. Then the support is [MATH: S = \{ 1,2,3,4 \},] and the corresponding probabilities are all [MATH: \dfrac{1}{4}{:}]

[MATH: f(1) = f(2) = f(3) = f(4) = \dfrac{1}{4}]

Summing up the products of each value of [MATH: X] and its associated probability, we get

[MATH: E[X]|= 1 ⋅ f(1) + 2 ⋅ f(2) + 3 ⋅ f(3) + 4 ⋅ f(4); = 1((1)/(4)) + 2((1)/(4)) + 3((1)/(4)) + 4((1)/(4)); = (1)/(4) + (2)/(4) + (3)/(4) + (4)/(4); = (1 + 2 + 3 + 4)/(4); = (10)/(4); = 2.5.]

items.title: Calculating the Expected Profit of a Game

sections.normalized_html: Suppose that we play a game with a stack of five cards labeled [MATH: 1] through [MATH: 5.] A card is drawn at random. Drawing [MATH: 1,2,3,] or [MATH: 4] means that you lose [MATH: \[math]1,] and drawing a [MATH: 5] means that you win [MATH: \[/math] 5.] What is the expected profit at each drawing in this game?
sections.readable_text: Suppose that we play a game with a stack of five cards labeled [MATH: 1] through [MATH: 5.] A card is drawn at random. Drawing [MATH: 1,2,3,] or [MATH: 4] means that you lose [MATH: \[math]1,] and drawing a [MATH: 5] means that you win [MATH: \[/math] 5.] What is the expected profit at each drawing in this game?

sections.normalized_html:
Let [MATH: p] represent the profit on a draw in this game. On each draw in the game, there are two possible outcomes:

  • drawing [MATH: 1,2,3,4], the player loses [MATH: \[math]1,] so we have [MATH: p=-1.]

  • drawing [MATH: 5], the player wins [MATH: \[/math]5,] so we have [MATH: p=5.]

The probabilities for the outcomes are [MATH: P(-1)=\dfrac{4}{5}, \qquad P(5)=\dfrac{1}{5}.]

Let's summarize this in a table. If [MATH: p] is the profit (in dollars) on a single draw, and [MATH: f(p)] is the probability mass function for [MATH: p,] then we have the following:

[MATH: p]

[MATH: -1]

[MATH: 5]

[MATH: f(p)]

[MATH: \dfrac{4}{5}]

[MATH: \dfrac{1}{5}]

Therefore, the expected value of [MATH: p] is given by

[MATH: \eqalign{ \textrm E[p] &= -1 \cdot f(-1) + 5 \cdot f(5) \[5pt] &= -1 \left( \dfrac{4}{5} \right) + 5 \left( \dfrac{1}{5} \right) \[5pt] &=-\dfrac{4}{5} + 1 \[3pt] &=\dfrac{1}{5} \[3pt] &=0.2 }]

Therefore, the expected profit at each draw in this game is [MATH: \[math]0.20].
sections.readable_text:

- drawing [MATH: 5], the player wins [MATH: \[/math]5,] so we have [MATH: p=5.]

The probabilities for the outcomes are
[MATH: P(-1)=\dfrac{4}{5}, \qquad P(5)=\dfrac{1}{5}.]

| [MATH: p] | [MATH: -1] | [MATH: 5] |
| [MATH: f(p)] | [MATH: \dfrac{4}{5}] | [MATH: \dfrac{1}{5}] |

Therefore, the expected value of [MATH: p] is given by

[MATH: \eqalign{
\textrm E[p] &= -1 \cdot f(-1) + 5 \cdot f(5) \[5pt]
&= -1 \left( \dfrac{4}{5} \right) + 5 \left( \dfrac{1}{5} \right) \[5pt]

lesson.readable_text:
Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
The expected value (also known as the expectation or mean) of a discrete random variable is the average value we'd expect to get if we observed the random variable many times.

Content:
For a discrete random variable [MATH: X] with probability mass function [MATH: f(x)] defined over a set [MATH: S,] we can calculate the expected value using the following formula:

Content:
[MATH: \textrm E[X] = \sum\limits_{x \in S} x \cdot f(x)]

Content:
In other words, the expected value is the sum of products of each value of [MATH: X] and its associated probability, taken over all possible values of [MATH: X.]

---

Item 2 — Example: Calculating the Expected Value for a Random Variable with Uniform Probability

Example Prompt:
What is the expected value of one roll of a tetrahedral die?

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
The expected value of a discrete random variable [MATH: X] with probability mass function [MATH: f(x)] defined over a set [MATH: S] is given by

[MATH: \textrm E[X] = \sum\limits_{x \in S} x \cdot f(x).]

A tetrahedral die has four sides. Let [MATH: X] be the score attained on a random roll of the die. Then the support is [MATH: S = \{ 1,2,3,4 \},] and the corresponding probabilities are all [MATH: \dfrac{1}{4}{:}]

[MATH: f(1) = f(2) = f(3) = f(4) = \dfrac{1}{4}]

Summing up the products of each value of [MATH: X] and its associated probability, we get

[MATH: E[X]|= 1 ⋅ f(1) + 2 ⋅ f(2) + 3 ⋅ f(3) + 4 ⋅ f(4); = 1((1)/(4)) + 2((1)/(4)) + 3((1)/(4)) + 4((1)/(4)); = (1)/(4) + (2)/(4) + (3)/(4) + (4)/(4); = (1 + 2 + 3 + 4)/(4); = (10)/(4); = 2.5.]

---

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
The expected value of a discrete random variable [MATH: X] with probability mass function [MATH: f(x)] defined over a set [MATH: S] is given by

[MATH: \textrm E[X] = \sum\limits_{x \in S} x \cdot f(x).]

Summing up the products of each value of [MATH: X] and its associated probability, we get

[MATH: E[X]|= 1 ⋅ f(1) + 2 ⋅ f(2) + 3 ⋅ f(3) + 4 ⋅ f(4); = 1((1)/(10)) + 2((3)/(10)) + 3((2)/(5)) + 4((1)/(5)); = (1)/(10) + (6)/(10) + (6)/(5) + (4)/(5); = (1)/(10) + (6)/(10) + (12)/(10) + (8)/(10); = (1 + 6 + 12 + 8)/(10); = (27)/(10); = 2.7.]

Item 8 — Example: Calculating the Expected Value Given the Frequency of a Random Variable

EXPLANATION

[MATH: \textrm E[X] = \sum\limits_{x \in S} x \cdot f(x).]

We're given the frequencies of the number of pets, so we can start by computing the corresponding probabilities. The total number of children is [MATH: 5+6+5=16,] so the corresponding probabilities are as follows:

[MATH: P(X = 0) = f(0)|= (5)/(16); P(X = 1) = f(1)|= (6)/(16) = (3)/(8); P(X = 2) = f(2)|= (5)/(16)]

We organize these results in the table below.

| [MATH: x] | [MATH: 0] | [MATH: 1] | [MATH: 2] |
| [MATH: f(x)] | [MATH: \dfrac{5}{16}] | [MATH: \dfrac{3}{8}] | [MATH: \dfrac{5}{16}] |

[MATH: E[X]|= 0 ⋅ f(0) + 1 ⋅ f(1) + 2 ⋅ f(2); = 0((5)/(16)) + 1((3)/(8)) + 2((5)/(16)); = 0 + (3)/(8) + (10)/(16); = 0 + (6)/(16) + (10)/(16); = (0 + 6 + 10)/(16); = (16)/(16); = 1.]
